correctness.rationale: For each q=2,3,4 the 81-shift autocorrelation identity and integer Eisenstein/Gaussian squared-norm formulas are exact. A free q^5 gauge normalizes five anchor coefficients; the eleven remaining digits are completely enumerated, 2048, 177147, and 4194304 cases. Exact minima, strict successor values, and normalized winner counts were recomputed from packaged checker.cpp with built-in expected-result assertions. Every equality word was independently cross-checked by the ordered-pair Fourier convolution identity. orbit_checker.py checked complete symmetry closures and two-orbit partition of the 240 and 24 exact winner lists. Supplemental 81-point Fourier quadrature checked each first representative. Nothing is inferred from partial sampling, and no unrestricted-complex claim is made.

residual_risks: Specialized, older, unindexed polyphase multidimensional array tables might contain equivalent sharp values or optimizer orbits; this is historical priority risk, not a proved novelty uniqueness guarantee.

value.rationale: The full 16-character Fourier unit cube is a canonical four-dimensional multi-index aperture, and ternary/quaternary PSK alphabets are natural choices for low-autocorrelation array design. The exact ternary penalty (384 versus binary 336) and quaternary recovery (336) give a mathematically meaningful nonnested-alphabet phenomenon, while two complete symmetry orbits in each nonbinary alphabet and strict next-energy gaps characterize the landscape rather than a single unmotivated numerical slice. The known binary benchmark motivates these specific missing cases; no general engineering gain is claimed.
